rules.quote: Use post-nominals in the correct order
rules.violation_condition: A person’s post-nominals appear in an order inconsistent with the specified category sequence or place a lower honour before a higher honour.
when: Applies when a person has multiple post-nominals.
The category sequence is honours and awards; KC, SC or JP; university degrees and diplomas; professional association memberships; parliamentary membership.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the category sequence and highest-honour condition in one ordering check; G-4 absorbs the body restatements.

rules.quote: full stops or spaces within post-nominals
rules.violation_condition: A post-nominal contains an internal full stop or space.
when: Applies within an individual post-nominal, not to spaces separating distinct post-nominals.
rules.why: The shared prohibition governs internal post-nominal formatting; commas at post-nominal boundaries are a separate check.

rules.violation_condition: A comma separates a person’s name from their post-nominals or separates adjacent post-nominals.
when: Applies to commas before the post-nominal sequence or between its members.
rules.why: G-2 combines the two prohibited comma positions because they are conditions of the same boundary-punctuation check.

covers.quote: Vice-regal and ecclesiastical titles and Australian Defence Force ranks usually precede all other titles.
Follow these with any other titles (such as ‘Dame’, ‘Sir’ and ‘Dr’) immediately before a person’s name.

rules.quote: Write titles before a person’s name in the correct order
rules.specification: The body specifies a default sequence, qualified by ‘usually’. It does not identify exceptions or specify precedence among vice-regal titles, ecclesiastical titles and Australian Defence Force ranks themselves.
rules.violation_condition: Titles before a person’s name depart from the default sequence of vice-regal or ecclesiastical titles and Australian Defence Force ranks before other titles, with those other titles immediately before the name.
when: Applies to titles preceding a person’s name.
Vice-regal and ecclesiastical titles and Australian Defence Force ranks usually precede all other titles.
Other titles, such as Dame, Sir and Dr, follow these and sit immediately before the person’s name.
rules.why: G-2 treats the title positions as one sequence check; G-4 absorbs the body’s elaboration rather than creating overlapping rules.
